items.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011
items.q: this one was a series of stories based on a character who they called “Nigger Charlie.”

ctx.x: But it’s not the right kind of vowel. It’s been a fascinating conversation. Any recording, studio recording memories you’ve had of doing things — let me rephrase. If you listen to the oldies station now these days, do you ever hear yourself with any of the Lou Rawls stuff, Tony Orlando, do you ever hear stuff you played on?

Well there was a recording that I did with Tony, which it’s a surprise because you almost never hear this thing, but Tony was trying to get into, and this was not good timing, into disco, while disco was dying. And so they made this disco recording and I had just joined the band. And for some reason they thought it was magic, he had to have me on this recording somewhere. And the road musicians don’t usually play on the recording, they have studio musicians who know how to make records rather than guys that play…

300? How does it enter the charts at 42? “Oh it’s very scientific. Very scientific.” Okay. Fine. So a couple of issues later it’s number thirty-something. 36 or 37. I said “you’re in the top 40.” I said great, I’m on a top 40 record. I hated it, but, I’m on a top 40 record. And then a couple of issues later he comes in and says “they pulled it.” I said “what do you mean they pulled it?” He said “it’s no longer in Billboard.” Out of 300 it was like 30 something, what happened? He said “oh it’s very scientific,…
